answer.text: Have a fixed maturity and are listed for secondary-market trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Close-ended mutual fund schemes have a fixed maturity (defined tenure set at launch) and, after the initial offer, their units are listed on a recognised stock exchange for secondary-market trading rather than being redeemable on demand from the fund. Investors looking to exit before maturity sell units on the exchange. The Trap: 'Accept redemptions daily' is the defining feature of open-ended funds, not close-ended ones. 'Unregulated' is incorrect — mutual funds (open or close-ended) operate under SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations. 'Invest only in gold' is a product category restriction, not a structural one. Note: The specific statement that close-ended mutual funds have a fixed maturity and are listed for secondary-market trading is not in the cited NISM Series XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook pages checked — those pages only contrast open-ended schemes with most funds allowing redemption. The framing above is presented as general industry / SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations knowledge rather than as a workbook citation.
